population: One locked corpus (live_corpus.v1.json) of 5 corpus cases exercised against the full 29-module canonical registry in module-manifest.json. 3 of the 5 cases are scored for full ScoreEnvelope byte parity (18 envelope fields each = 54 field comparisons); 4 cases exercise the module-owned error-taxonomy Display-string rows; 3 cases exercise lane-reachability; every envelope carries 7 audited claim locks. This is a small, hand-curated differential-testing corpus (McKeeman 1998), not a sampled or powered statistical population -- the KPI floor is exact byte parity (1.0), not a confidence interval.
split_methodology: No fitting, no train/test split. The CPython oracle is pure Python with zero Rust linkage, predicting envelope bytes from module-manifest.json plus the published minimum-privilege spec; ground truth is stdout of a separately compiled release binary linking the real amphora-engine crate as a path dependency (no logic copied). Agreement is a cross-implementation differential check in the sense of McKeeman 1998, not a self-comparison. Every run executes the compiled probe twice (two-replay) and requires byte-identical stdout before any gate is evaluated.
theory: Saltzer & Schroeder 1975, Proc. IEEE 63(9), DOI 10.1109/PROC.1975.9939 -- least privilege, fail-safe defaults. McKeeman 1998, Digital Technical Journal 10(1):100-107 -- differential testing. Denning 1976, CACM 19(5), DOI 10.1145/360051.360056 -- lattice model of secure information flow, carried from the sibling authority-lattice-completeness-v1 audit that this live-runtime probe closes the gap named in.
